subject: physics

concepts.title: Electric Current
concepts.definition: The rate of net charge flow through a given cross-sectional area of a conductor over a specific time interval.
concepts.key_idea: Current measures the flow of net charge per unit time.
question_patterns: calculate the current flowing through a conductor
find the net charge passing in a given time
what is the current if charge q flows in time t
determine the rate of charge flow
how much current is produced by the charge flow

solution_steps.explain: current is defined as the ratio of net charge to time interval

concepts.title: Resistance and Ohms Law
concepts.definition: The ratio of potential difference across a conductor to the current flowing through it, representing the opposition to charge flow.
concepts.key_idea: Resistance is the constant of proportionality between voltage and current in ohmic conductors.
question_patterns: find the resistance of a conductor
calculate the resistance given voltage and current
what is the resistance if potential difference is v and current is i
determine the resistance of the heating element
how much resistance does the circuit offer

concepts.title: Resistivity of a Conductor
concepts.definition: A material-specific property relating resistance to the physical dimensions of a conductor, specifically length and cross-sectional area.
concepts.key_idea: Resistivity depends on the material, not the dimensions of the conductor.
question_patterns: calculate the resistivity of the material
find the resistivity given resistance length and area
what is the resistivity of the wire
determine the material property resistivity
how much is the resistivity for a conductor of given dimensions

concepts.title: Electrical Power Dissipation
concepts.definition: The rate at which electrical energy is converted into heat within a conductor due to current flow.
concepts.key_idea: Power loss in a resistor is the product of current and potential difference.
question_patterns: calculate the power dissipated in the resistor
find the power consumed by the device
what is the electrical power loss
determine the power given current and voltage
how much power is dissipated as heat

solution_steps.explain: power is the product of current and voltage

worked_examples.question_pattern: if {charge} Coulombs flow in {time} seconds find current
calculate resistance for {voltage} Volts and {current} Amperes

questions: A wire of length 15 m and area 6.0e-7 m2 has resistance 5.0 Ohm. Find resistivity.
